name: If We Talked Like This Everywhere
why_it_works: Putting stiff industry talk into an everyday moment like ordering coffee is a register clash: the wrong voice in the wrong room is instantly funny, and viewers recognize how jargon made them feel. Ending with the promise to speak plainly makes the brand the one pro who doesn't talk like that to you.

hook.pattern: Show your team using industry jargon in ordinary places where it plainly does not belong.
examples: If we talked like {{industry}} people everywhere.
We tried {{industry}} talk at a coffee shop. Bad idea.
What {{industry}} jargon sounds like in real life.

variables.name: industry
variables.description: The field, as customers say it (2 words or fewer)

variables.name: jargon_coffee
variables.description: Ordering coffee, said entirely in industry jargon; must still use the terms correctly (18 words or fewer)
variables.example: One latte, please. Pending final underwriting of the oat milk. I'll lock the price for 30 days.

variables.name: jargon_date
variables.description: A first-date line said in industry jargon, harmless and not about the other person's body or money habits (18 words or fewer)
variables.example: Before dessert, I'll need two years of your favorite movies and a full playlist history.

variables.name: jargon_party
variables.description: A kid's birthday party line in jargon, the biggest of the three (18 words or fewer)
variables.example: The cake has cleared underwriting. Candles are subject to appraisal. Closing on the piñata is Saturday.

variables.name: jargon_self_own
variables.description: The team using jargon on itself at the office, self-deprecating (18 words or fewer)
variables.example: Lunch is in escrow until Dave confirms the order. Dave has not confirmed the order.

variables.name: plain_promise
variables.description: The real, plain-language promise to clients, as a process not a result (15 words or fewer)
variables.example: Every word in your paperwork explained before you sign. Every time.

variables.name: decoder_term
variables.description: One jargon word the viewer will actually hear from you

variables.name: decoder_meaning
variables.description: Its correct plain meaning plus what to ask about it (20 words or fewer)
variables.example: Your rate is held for a set number of days. Ask how many, and what happens after.

variables.name: offer
variables.description: What the viewer gets for acting (10 words or fewer)

variables.name: disclosure
variables.description: Required fine print for the client's niche, copied from the matching pack in compliance/packs.json

slides.headline: If we talked like this everywhere
slides.body: A public service announcement from {{brand}}. Swipe carefully.
slides.visual_prompt: 4:5 bold title card in {{brand}} colors, a serious office memo look with a big red stamp reading OFF THE CLOCK

slides.headline: At the coffee shop
slides.visual_prompt: 4:5 candid photo of a person in business clothes ordering at a coffee counter with total seriousness, the barista blinking, warm cafe light

slides.headline: On a first date
slides.visual_prompt: 4:5 photo of a candlelit restaurant table, one person sliding a neat folder of forms across to their puzzled date, warm romantic light

slides.headline: At a kid's birthday party
slides.visual_prompt: 4:5 bright backyard birthday party, an adult in a blazer holding a clipboard next to the cake, balloons, kids laughing in soft focus

slides.headline: At our own office
slides.body: "{{jargon_self_own}}" We do it to each other too.
slides.visual_prompt: 4:5 candid photo inside {{brand}}, team members around a desk staring at an empty lunch order screen, natural office light, playful

slides.headline: With you, we switch it off
slides.visual_prompt: 4:5 warm candid photo of a team member from {{brand}} explaining a printed page to a client across a desk, both smiling, natural light

slides.headline: The one word worth knowing
slides.body: {{decoder_term}}: {{decoder_meaning}} Save this for your first meeting.
slides.visual_prompt: 4:5 clean note card with the word in bold serif type and a short plain explanation, {{brand}} accent color, save-worthy layout

slides.headline: Talk to a human
slides.visual_prompt: 4:5 clean end card on {{brand}} brand color, logo, offer text in large friendly type, a small speech bubble icon

cta: Which word has confused you most? Ask us, then book {{offer}}.

craft.technique: Register clash: industry jargon used in everyday places (fish-out-of-water)
craft.notes: Setup: the title card frames it as a public service announcement, so the reader expects one thing and gets jargon in a coffee shop. Escalation: three everyday rooms climb from coffee to a date to a kid's party, each line delivered with total seriousness; the jargon must be used correctly, because accurate words in the wrong room is the joke. Turn: the team turns the jargon on itself at the office ('Dave has not confirmed the order'), a self-own that earns trust. Tag: the switch-off slide states the plain promise, and the decoder slide gives one useful word so the carousel is worth saving. Timing in a carousel lives in the swipe: put the most absurd word last in each line so the swipe is the pause.

do_not: Use a jargon term incorrectly just to get a laugh; the terms must stay accurate
Make any line about the other person's looks, money habits or credit
Mock clients who didn't know a word; the joke is on the jargon and the team
Give personalized advice in any slide
compliance: Mortgage: definitions are general education, not a rate offer; no rate, payment or approval promises; show NMLS ID and Equal Housing Opportunity on the end card
Law firms: definitions are general information, not legal advice; label as attorney advertising where your state bar requires
Financial advisors: no return or performance claims inside any definition; include required firm disclosures in the caption
Insurance: definitions must not imply any specific coverage; add 'coverage varies by policy and state'
Have a licensed professional at the business check every definition for accuracy before posting
